title: The Bandits' Toll
text: A rope across the road, hung with bells, and three bandits behind it. They are very polite and very well armed, and their coats once belonged to better people. A toll, they say, for the road's upkeep. Nobody has kept up this road in a hundred years.

options.label: Pay their toll and smile, and save your blades for worthier foes.

outcomes.text: They lift the rope with a bow and a jingle of bells, and count your coin very carefully, and watch you go.

options.label: The best talker talks them down, with silver words instead of silver coin.

outcomes.text: By the end they are paying you to leave, and not quite sure why.
They are not persuaded. Their smiles stay, but their hands move toward their blades.

options.label: Cut the rope and see what they do. No one tolls this road but you.

outcomes.text: Three bandits, and their friends in the trees, and they were always going to do this whatever you paid.
